 JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the death of D.Girija W/o Late Venkataramana .D, in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is the specific case of the petitioners that on 19-10-2011 at about 7.15 p.m., the deceased Girija was riding a Scooty bearing No.KA-05-EM-9277 near Devinagar Bridge, Ring Road, Devinagar,
Bengaluru.

At that time, the driver of Lorry bearing registration No.KA-06-C-3437 (hereinafter referred to as the "offending vehicle"), drove the same at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the scooty.
3. Due to the impact, the deceased was thrown to the ground and sustained grievous injuries all over her body and succumbed to the injuries.
Thereafter, the Post-mortem examination was conducted at M.S.Ramaiah hospital, Bengaluru and subsequently the dead body was handed over to the petitioners, who performed the last rites.
The petitioners submit that they incurred expenses of about Rs. 25,000/- towards transportation, funeral, and obsequies.
It is further submitted that the accident and resultant death of Girija occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry.
At the time of the accident, the deceased was aged 45 years and working as a Beautician, earning a monthly income of about Rs.10,000/-.
4. The petitioners contend that they were entirely dependent upon the income of the deceased.

Petitioner No. 1 and 2 being the children of the deceased, have suffered immense mental shock,
agony, emotional trauma, and loss of their breadwinner as well as moral support.

Hence, the petitioners have prayed for award of compensation of Rs. 10,00,000/- with interest, jointly and severally, from Respondent No. 1 - the insurer of the offending vehicle, and Respondent No. 2 - the insured.
5. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsels and filed their written statements respectively.
6. Respondent No.1, the insurer of the offending vehicle, has filed its objection statement.
It has admitted the issuance of an insurance policy in favour of Respondent No.2 and its validity as on the date of the accident.

However, it has contended that its liability, if any, is subject to the terms,

2 conditions and limitations of the said policy.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 has specifically denied that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and has instead contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased herself.

On that premise,
it is contended that the owner and insurer of the motorcycle are proper and necessary parties to the proceedings.

It is further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of the accident and that the police have filed a charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under Section 3 read with Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Respondent No.1 has also specifically disputed the age, avocation and income of the deceased and has denied the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased as well as the dependency claimed in the petition.
On these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

7. Respondent No.2, the registered owner of the offending vehicle, has filed his written statement admitting that he is the registered owner of the said vehicle and stating that the vehicle was duly insured with Respondent No.1 under a valid and effective insurance policy as on the date of the accident.

He has specifically denied that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence and carelessness of the deceased herself.

He has denied the other averments made in the petition and,
on these grounds, has sought dismissal of the claim petition as against him.

8. It is further on record that Respondent No.2 did not initially contest the case and, after this Tribunal fixed liability against Respondent No.1, the same was challenged before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, which remanded the matter with a direction to afford a fresh opportunity to Respondent No.2 to adduce evidence.
Pursuant thereto, this Tribunal has granted opportunity to all parties to lead their evidence.

Thereafter, Respondent No.2 has filed an additional statement of objections contending that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased, as she was riding the scooter without holding a valid driving licence.

He has further reiterated that the offending vehicle was insured with Respondent No.1 under a valid policy as on the date of the accident and that the driver of the offending vehicle was holding a valid and effective driving licence at the relevant point of time, which was subsequently renewed.

Therefore, it is contended that in the event of any compensation being awarded by this Tribunal, Respondent No.1 alone is liable to indemnify the same, and accordingly, Respondent No.2 has prayed for dismissal of the petition as against him.
9.

On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that they are the legal representatives of deceased Smt.Girija ?

2. Whether the petitioner proves that on 19.10.2011 at about 7.15 p.m. when the deceasd was riding Scooty bearing No.KA 05 EM 9277 slowly and cautiously on the Ring Road near Devinagara Bridge, Bengaluru at that time the driver of lorry bearing No.KA 06 C 3437 had come at high speed in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed against the moped and due to the impact the Arun Kumar @ Arun vs Oicl on 23 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62228707/
3 deceased had sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same on the spot?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom ?
4. What order or award ?

Additional Issue:
1. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and as such it is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners by indemnifying the respondent No.2 ?
10.
In support of their claim, Petitioner No.1 was examined as PW-1 and documents were marked on behalf of the petitioners as Exhibits P-1 to P-10.

Initially, Respondent No.1, the Insurance Company,
examined its official as RW-1 and marked documents as Exhibits R-1 and R-2.

After the matter was remanded, Respondent No.1 submitted that the official earlier examined as RW-1 had left its service and , therefore, was unable to tender himself for cross- examination before this court.

Consequently,
respondent no 1 sought permission to examine another authorized official to substantiate its contentions.
Accordingly, this Tribunal permitted the same, and the authorized official of Respondent No.1 was examined as RW-2, and his authorization letter was marked as Exhibit R-3.
Further, Respondent No.2, the owner of the offending vehicle, was examined as RW-3 and the true copy of the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle was marked as Exhibit R-4.
11. After remand by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, a fresh opportunity was afforded to the parties to substantiate their respective versions.
This Tribunal has heard the learned counsel appearing for all the parties and perused the material available on record.

12. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : Partly In the Affirmative.
Addl.Issue No 1:In the Negative.
Issue No.4 :

As per the final order,
for the following:
REASONS 13. ISSUE NO.1:- The petitioners have claimed that they are the legal heirs of the deceased.
Petitioner No.1, who was examined as PW-1, has filed his affidavit stating that he is the son of the deceased and that Petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased.
In support of the said claim, the ration card has been produced and marked as Exhibit P-8.
On perusal of the material on record, it is evident from the inquest report that Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are the children of the deceased.

The respondents have not disputed the relationship or the status of the petitioners as legal heirs of the deceased, nor has any contrary evidence been placed on record or any rival claimant come forward.

sentences.text: In the absence of any rebuttal evidence, the material available on record is sufficient to hold that the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is answered in affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.2:- Petitioner No.1, who is the son of the deceased, entered the witness box and was examined as PW-1.

He filed his affidavit in lieu of examination-in-chief under Order XVIII Rule 4 of the CPC, reiterating the averments made in the claim petition and stating that on 19-10-2011 at about 7.15 p.m., the deceased Girija was riding a Scooty bearing No.KA-05-EM-9277 near Devinagar Bridge, Ring Road, Devinagar, Bengaluru.

At that time, the driver of Lorry bearing registration No.KA-06-C-3437 (hereinafter referred to as the "offending vehicle"), drove the same at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the scooty.
Due to the impact, the deceased was thrown to the ground and sustained grievous injuries all over her body and succumbed to the injuries.
15. He produced the police records, which were marked as Exhibits P-1 to P-10.
Exhibit P-1 is the FIR registered on the basis of his first information statement.
Exhibit P-2 is the statement of witnesses.
Exhibit P-3 is the spot sketch.
Exhibit P-4 is the spot mahazar, Exhibit P-5 is the charge sheet.
Exhibit P-6 is the IMV report.
Exhibit P-7 is the inquest report, and Exhibit P-10 is the post-mortem report.
The charge sheet filed by the Investigating Officer squarely fixes the responsibility for the accident on the driver of the offending lorry.
Exhibits P-3 and P-4, namely the sketch and spot mahazar prepared by the Investigating Officer, clearly corroborate the manner and place of the accident.
16. During the course of cross-examination, a suggestion was made by the learned counsel for the respondents that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased herself.
PW-1 categorically denied the said suggestion.
Except this suggestion, nothing material was elicited in the cross-examination to discredit his testimony or to shake his version of the occurrence.

17. Though the officials of Respondent No.1 was examined as RW-1 and RW2 and the owner of the offending lorry was examined as RW-3, their evidence is only in reiteration of the averments made in their written statements and is not supported by any independent or documentary evidence.
Significantly, no credible evidence was adduced by the respondents to substantiate their plea.

No independent witnesses were examined and, more importantly, if the accident had not occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending lorry, the respondents ought to have examined the driver of the offending vehicle, produced contrary investigation records, or taken appropriate steps to challenge the charge sheet filed by the police.
No such steps were taken.

18. It is a well-settled principle that in motor accident claim proceedings, the standard of proof is not proof beyond reasonable doubt as in criminal trials, but proof on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.

Applying this principle, the oral testimony of PW-1, coupled with the contemporaneous police records such as the FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, charge sheet,
IMV report and inquest clearly establishes that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry, resulting in the death of Girija.

Accordingly,
this Tribunal holds that the petitioners have successfully proved Issue No.1, and the same is answered in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Addl. Issue No.1:

The Respondent No. 1- Insurance Company has contended that there was a violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy on the ground that the offending vehicle was a lorry, a transport vehicle, and that the driver of the said lorry did not possess a valid and effective transport driving licence as on the date of the accident.

It is further contended that, in the absence of a valid and effective driving licence, Respondent No. 1 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner and is absolved from indemnifying the owner of the offending vehicle.
20. In order to substantiate the said contention, Respondent No. 1 has examined its officials as RW1 and RW2, who have reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
On the other hand, the owner of the offending lorry was examined as RW3, and he has produced Exhibit D4, the driving licence of the driver of the offending lorry.

On perusal of Exhibit D4, it reveals that the driver was holding a driving licence for non-transport vehicles from 18-05-1998 to 18-05- 2018, and that he had obtained a transport vehicle driving licence on 10-12-1999.
21.

While filing the additional written statement, Respondent No. 1 has placed reliance on a photocopy of the driving licence extract; however, the same was not marked in evidence as it was only a photocopy.
Even on perusal of the said extract, it appears that the transport vehicle driving licence was subsequently renewed.
It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 19-10-2011 and that the driving licence was renewed on 22-12-2011, i.e., after a lapse of about two months from the date of the accident.
During the course of cross-examination, the learned counsel for Respondent No. 1 has specifically elicited this fact.
22. However, there is no material on record to show that the driver was disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence or that his licence was suspended for any violation of law.

Respondent No. 1 has failed to substantiate its contention that, as on the date of the accident, the driver of the offending lorry was disqualified from driving the vehicle or that his licence stood suspended.

23. The learned counsel for Respondent No. 2 has placed reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in:
1) MFA.No.8599/2013 (MV-D) - Sri.Manjunath Vs. Smt.Gangamma and others.
2) MFA. No. 103680/2015 (MV-D) C/w MFA. No. 103681/2015 - Nagappa @
Nagaraja and others Vs. Ravi Kupaluru and others.
3) MFA.No.6099/2012 (MV) - Sri.K.U.Appaiah Vs. Master Sanoof and another.
4) MFA.No.3892/2014 (MV-I) - Pascal Dias Vs. Srinivas D Kamath and others.
5) (2004) 3 SCC 297 - National Ins.Co.Ltd., Vs. Swaran Singh and others.
24.

On careful perusal of the said decisions, it is clear that where the driving licence is subsequently renewed and there is no disqualification or suspension, the insurer cannot avoid its liability merely Arun Kumar @ Arun vs Oicl on 23 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62228707/
6 on the ground that the licence had expired prior to the accident.

sentences.text: Once the driving licence is renewed without any endorsement of suspension or disqualification, such renewal relates back, and the insurer remains liable to satisfy the award.

25. In the present case, though the driving licence was renewed after the accident, there is no evidence to show that the driver was disqualified from driving the class of vehicle involved or that his licence was suspended for any statutory violation.
The renewal was granted without imposing any condition or restriction, which clearly indicates that the licensing authority found the driver competent to hold a valid driving licence.

26. Therefore, in view of the principles laid down in the above said decisions, it is held that as on the date of the accident, the driver of the offending lorry was not disqualified from holding a driving licence, and the subsequent renewal validates his entitlement to drive the vehicle.
Consequently, the contention of Respondent No. 1 that there was a fundamental breach of policy conditions cannot be accepted.

27. Accordingly, Respondent No. 1-Insurance Company cannot escape from its liability by merely contending that the driver did not possess a valid and effective driving licence on the date of the accident.
Hence, Respondent No. 1 is held liable to indemnify the owner of the offending vehicle and to satisfy the award.
With these observation, I answer Additional issue No.1 in the Negative.
28. ISSUE No.3:
The petitioners have stated in their claim petition that the deceased was aged 45 years at the time of the accident.
Ex. P9, the DL of the deceased, clearly mentions her date of birth as 31-07- 1969.
Accordingly, the age of the deceased is taken as 42 years as on the date of accident and the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 14 for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
29. The petitioner claimed that the deceased Girija was a Beautician and earning a monthly income of about Rs.10,000/-.
The Petitioners are financial and emotionally dependents on the deceased.
Due to her untimely death, they have suffered immense mental shock, agony and loss of the sole breadwinner of the family.
To substantiate the income and avocation of the deceased, the Petitioners have not produced any supportive documents.
In the absence of proof of income, this tribunal is of the opinion that the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2011, notional income Rs.6,500/- per month is taken for the assessment of compensation.
30. As the deceased is below 50 years, 25% future prospects is to be added.
Then the income would be 8,125/-.

As there are 2 dependents, 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards her personal and living expenses and the annual income would come to (8,125 -2,708 =5,417) (Rs.5,417 X 12)
Rs.65,004/- and applying 14 multiplier
, Petitioners are awarded Rs.9,10,056/- towards loss of dependency.
31. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1, this Tribunal deems it Arun Kumar @ Arun vs Oicl on 23 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62228707/
7 proper to hold that the Petitioners are entitled Rs.20,000/- each under the head of consortium as Petitioner No.1 and 2 have lost their mother.

32. Loss to estate:
The loss to the estate is the loss of savings by the deceased.
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 and 2 have lost their mother.
Hence, Rs.10,000/- towards loss to estate.
33. Transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses:
Petitioners have claimed that they have spent Rs.25,000/- towards transportation of 1 dead body, funeral & obsequies and other incidental expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award Rs.10,000/- for the transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses.

sentences.text: However, this Court has already held under Issue No. 1 and Additional Issue No.1 that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending lorry.

Further, while answering Additional Issue No. 1,
this Court has categorically held that, as on the date of the accident, the driver of the offending lorry was not disqualified from holding a valid driving licence and that the Insurance Company cannot escape from its liability merely on the ground that the driving licence had expired and was renewed subsequently.
36. In view of the said finding, there is no breach of policy conditions on the part of the insured.
Consequently, the doctrine of pay and recovery does not arise for consideration in the present case.
37. The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and insured of the offending lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% per annum.

18. It is a well-settled principle that in motor accident claim proceedings, the standard of proof is not proof beyond reasonable doubt as in criminal trials, but proof on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Applying this principle, the oral testimony of PW-1, coupled with the contemporaneous police records such as the FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, charge sheet,
IMV report and inquest clearly establishes that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry, resulting in the death of Girija.
The Respondent No. 1- Insurance Company has contended that there was a violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy on the ground that the offending vehicle was a lorry, a transport vehicle, and that the driver of the said lorry did not possess a valid and effective transport driving licence as on the date of the accident.
22. However, there is no material on record to show that the driver was disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence or that his licence was suspended for any violation of law.
Respondent No. 1 has failed to substantiate its contention that, as on the date of the accident, the driver of the offending lorry was disqualified from driving the vehicle or that his licence stood suspended.
On careful perusal of the said decisions, it is clear that where the driving licence is subsequently renewed and there is no disqualification or suspension, the insurer cannot avoid its liability merely Arun Kumar @ Arun vs Oicl on 23 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62228707/
6 on the ground that the licence had expired prior to the accident.
Once the driving licence is renewed without any endorsement of suspension or disqualification, such renewal relates back, and the insurer remains liable to satisfy the award.
25. In the present case, though the driving licence was renewed after the accident, there is no evidence to show that the driver was disqualified from driving the class of vehicle involved or that his licence was suspended for any statutory violation.
The renewal was granted without imposing any condition or restriction, which clearly indicates that the licensing authority found the driver competent to hold a valid driving licence.
Hence, Respondent No. 1 is held liable to indemnify the owner of the offending vehicle and to satisfy the award.
The petitioners have relied upon various decision i.e., 2025 AHC 14110 - ICICI Lombard Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd., Vs. Smt.Arti Devi and 8 others, (2018) 9 SC 650 - Shamanna and another Vs. Divisional Manger, Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd., and others and (2018) 3 SCC 208 - Pappu and others Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another, in support of the principle of pay and recovery.

, Petitioners are awarded Rs.9,10,056/- towards loss of dependency.

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1, this Tribunal deems it Arun Kumar @ Arun vs Oicl on 23 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62228707/
7 proper to hold that the Petitioners are entitled Rs.20,000/- each under the head of consortium as Petitioner No.1 and 2 have lost their mother.
Total Rs.40,000/- is awarded towards loss of consortium.
32. Loss to estate:
The loss to the estate is the loss of savings by the deceased.
Hence, Rs.10,000/- towards loss to estate.
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award Rs.10,000/- for the transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies expenses.

Hence, the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and insured of the offending lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% per annum.
In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to above Issues,
I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioners are awarded compensation of .9,70,056/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of amount, 50% each of the amount is apportioned to the Petitioner No.1 and 2.
The entire apportioned amount with interest in respect of Petitioner No.1 and 2 shall be disbursed to them through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
